question: In the pulverized-coal boiler co-firing 20% ammonia, what CO2, CO and NO changes does post-flame ammonia injection give, and what NO change does burnout-zone injection give?
expect: post-flame: CO2 -33%, CO -80%, NO about +88%; burnout zone: NO about +571% (abstract)
rendered:
According to the document, post-flame injection of ammonia in the 20% co-firing case results in the lowest normalized CO2 and CO concentrations, corresponding to reductions of 33.0% and 80.47%, respectively. However, the outlet NO concentration increases by 87.88% compared to pure-coal firing.

Burnout-zone injection of ammonia in the 20% co-firing case results in a higher NO peak in the burnout zone, with a normalized value of 6.79, much higher than in other cases, and remains elevated downstream to the furnace exit.
